detailed_results.answer:
The context-free network (CFN) solves jigsaw puzzles by receiving shuffled image patches through siamese convolutional layers with shared weights and predicting the correct spatial permutation index. [Self_Supervised_Learning_Review_Paper.pdf, p. 2].

Sources:
- Self_Supervised_Learning_Review_Paper.pdf (page 2)

Masked Autoencoders (MAE) mask a high proportion (e.g. 75%) of image patches during pretraining and use an asymmetric encoder-decoder to reconstruct missing pixels, scaling efficiently with large vision transformers. [Self_Supervised_Learning_Review_Paper.pdf, p. 3].

Sources:
- Self_Supervised_Learning_Review_Paper.pdf (page 3)

The timeline illustrates major milestones including pretext tasks (jigsaw puzzles, colorization), contrastive learning (SimCLR, MoCo), and masked autoencoding architectures (MAE). [Self_Supervised_Learning_Review_Paper.pdf, p. 4].

Sources:
- Self_Supervised_Learning_Review_Paper.pdf (page 4)

DINOv2 frozen features achieve strong competitive performance on dense downstream tasks such as semantic segmentation and monocular depth estimation without requiring fine-tuning of the backbone. [Self_Supervised_Learning_Review_Paper.pdf, p. 5].

Sources:
- Self_Supervised_Learning_Review_Paper.pdf (page 5)

I-JEPA predicts representations directly in latent feature space rather than pixel space, avoiding costly pixel-level reconstruction and learning more semantic abstract representations. [Self_Supervised_Learning_Review_Paper.pdf, p. 6].

Sources:
- Self_Supervised_Learning_Review_Paper.pdf (page 6)

SimCLR maximizes similarity between differently augmented views of the same image while minimizing similarity to views of other images in the latent representation space. [Self_Supervised_Learning_Review_Paper.pdf, p. 3].

Sources:
- Self_Supervised_Learning_Review_Paper.pdf (page 3)

MoCo maintains a dynamic queue of negative samples and updates the key encoder via a momentum coefficient to ensure slowly evolving, consistent representations. [Self_Supervised_Learning_Review_Paper.pdf, p. 3].

Sources:
- Self_Supervised_Learning_Review_Paper.pdf (page 3)

Siamese networks process multiple image patches in parallel using identical weight parameters to extract consistent spatial feature embeddings before permutation classification. [Self_Supervised_Learning_Review_Paper.pdf, p. 2].

Sources:
- Self_Supervised_Learning_Review_Paper.pdf (page 2)

MAE typically splits images into regular patches such as 16x16 pixels and applies a high masking ratio of around 75% to prevent trivial interpolation. [Self_Supervised_Learning_Review_Paper.pdf, p. 3].

Sources:
- Self_Supervised_Learning_Review_Paper.pdf (page 3)

Self-supervised pretraining produces richer, more transferable representations that avoid overfitting to specific label sets, enhancing generalization and out-of-distribution robustness. [Self_Supervised_Learning_Review_Paper.pdf, p. 5].

Sources:
- Self_Supervised_Learning_Review_Paper.pdf (page 5)
